To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effect of looseness of bolts on the structural behaviour of bonded-butted butt joints is significant and should be considered in design.
the loss of bolt tension due to looseness of the fastener has an important effect on the deformation characteristics of bonded-bolt steel butt joints subjected to inplane bending.
the loss of bolt preload has a significant effect on the structural behaviour of bonded-boltted steel butt joints.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects of the behaviour of bonded-boltted steel butt joints: (i) the effect of looseness of bolts on the structural behaviour, (ii) the effect of the number of bolts and their distribution on the structural behaviour and (iii) the effect of pre-stress on the structural behaviour of the joint.
the development of an understanding of the behaviour of bonded-bolts joints and the effect of looseness on the structural performance.
the effect of bolt looseness to the structural behaviour of bonded-bolts steel butt joints.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the loss of bolt preload does not significantly affect the structural integrity and behaviour of bonded-but jointed structures, provided that the bolts are not fully loose.
the loss of bolt preload has a significant effect on the in-plane behaviour of the bonded-bolted joint, and this effect becomes more pronounced as the joint is loaded to higher bending moment.
bolt looseness does not have a significant effect on the deformation characteristics of bonded-bolt steel butt joints.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the loss of the bolt tightness has a significant influence to the deformation characteristics of the bonded-bolted joint and the magnitude of this influence is dependent on the magnitude of the applied bending moment.
the looseness of the bolted joints can be classified into three categories: (i) bolted joint without looseness (ii) bolted joint with partial looseness and (iii) bolted joint completely loose.
the loss of the bolts’ tightness has a significant effect to the structural behaviour of the joint, and this effect is more pronounced when the joint is loaded in the plane of the bolts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the loss of bolt preload can have a dramatic effect on the inplane deformation behaviour of bonded-bolts butt joints.

the loss of bolt tension due to bolt loosenesses results in a decrease of the joint stiffness, which is more pronounced for the joint under the bending moment about the minor axis than the major axis.
the effect of bolt looseness is to reduce the inplane bending capacity of the joint by a factor of about 2.5, but the effect on the out of plane bending capacity is not significant.
